one_liner: CUDA NUFFT gridding/degridding hard-wired for 2D radial MRI trajectories; paper reports 6-30x over gpuNUFFT, BART and IRT.
what_it_does: A command-line CUDA program (tron) that grids radial (linear or golden-angle) multi-coil k-space data onto a Cartesian grid and runs cuFFT to get images (adjoint, -a), or degrids an image into radial samples (forward). Input and output are the author's .ra raw-array files; the kernels and recon_radial_2d are extern "C" but all configuration lives in static globals set by main(), so it is a research tool rather than a callable library. It also handles sliding-window/helical slice stacks (-d) and undersampled data (-u); it reconstructs single 2D slices with a sum-of-squares coil combine.
how_it_is_fast: The trajectory is computed analytically inside the kernels (angle = pe*pi/npe or the golden-angle increment), so no trajectory array, presorting or atomic scatter is needed: in gridding each thread owns one Cartesian point (4x4 tiled thread mapping) and gathers, over every spoke, only the radial samples inside a circular band of +/- kernel width around its radius. Density compensation is an analytic ramp (precompensate kernel) instead of an iterative DCF, the Kaiser-Bessel kernel is evaluated on the fly with a polynomial I0 approximation, and float32 math is built with --use_fast_math; cuFFT does the oversampled (2x default) FFT.
when_to_use: Offline or real-time reconstruction of 2D radial MRI (uniform-angle or golden-angle), including stack-of-stars and sliding-window golden-angle series on one Nvidia GPU.
As a reference design for trajectory-specialised gridding: the 995-line tron.cu shows the gather-with-analytic-trajectory approach that beat general GPU gridders in the MRM 2019 paper.
Reproducing or extending the MRM 2019 comparison against gpuNUFFT, BART and Fessler's IRT (scripts RUNME1-4 plus git-lfs data).
Square-image adjoint NUFFT where single precision and a fixed Kaiser-Bessel kernel are acceptable.
when_not_to_use: Arbitrary, spiral or 3D trajectories: only 2D radial is implemented (a -3 'koosh' flag exists but the kernels are 2D); issue #7 asking how to add other trajectories is unanswered since Nov 2024. Use a general NUFFT (cuFINUFFT, gpuNUFFT, BART) instead.
More than 6 coil channels times repetitions: per-thread accumulators are float2 utmp[MAXCHAN] with MAXCHAN hard-coded to 6, and nothing checks nc*nt against it.
Iterative reconstruction: the CGNR path (-i) is commented 'NOT WORKING CORRECTLY YET' in tron.cu.
Non-square images, double precision, multi-GPU (MULTI_GPU is compiled to 0) or use as an in-process library with several concurrent plans (global static state).
Production builds on current toolchains without porting: the Makefile pins nvcc -ccbin gcc-6 and the CUDA code dates from 2018-2021.

integration.form: source-drop (CUDA command-line program built with a Makefile)
integration.dependencies: CUDA toolkit with cuFFT and cuBLAS; reproduction also needs MATLAB, gpuNUFFT, BART and git-lfs data
integration.min_toolchain: nvcc with gcc-6 host compiler as written in src/Makefile; minimum CUDA version not documented
integration.platforms: Linux/Unix with an Nvidia CUDA GPU (single GPU); POSIX headers (unistd.h, err.h) used
integration.thread_safety: Not thread-safe: plans, streams, device buffers and recon parameters are file-scope static globals; not documented otherwise

gotchas: Channel count is capped silently: gridradial2d accumulates into a fixed 6-element per-thread array while looping over nc*nt channels, so larger coil arrays overflow it; compress coils to <=6 first.

The built-in 'Elapsed time' uses clock() (process CPU time) around the whole recon including cuFFT plan creation, allocation and host transfers, not CUDA events; do not compare it directly with kernel-only timings.
Image size is derived from the readout (nx = ny = nro/2) and images must be square; the pad kernel's '> 0' bounds test drops source row/column 0 in the forward (degridding) path.
cudaFreeHost(&h_outdata) passes the address of the pointer instead of the pointer at exit, so the pinned buffer is not freed correctly (harmless for the CLI, wrong if reused as library code).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: FINUFFT/cuFINUFFT is the general-purpose choice (any trajectory, 1-3D, double precision, maintained library API); pick TRON only when data are strictly 2D radial on an Nvidia GPU and you want the trajectory-specialised, presort-free gather approach, noting that TRON's paper (2019) predates cuFINUFFT and never compared against it. The other FFT siblings (cuFFT alternatives such as VkFFT, tcFFT, TurboFFT) are uniform FFTs and do not address non-Cartesian gridding.
verified_claims_summary: The README claims 30x over gpuNUFFT and 75x over Fessler's CPU MATLAB IRT for radial gridding; the peer-reviewed MRM 2019 abstract (seen only via search summaries) gives 6-30x over the closest competitor depending on data set and calls TRON the most accurate code tested. Built with nvcc -O3 --use_fast_math against cuFFT; the GPU model and CUDA version are not stated on any page opened.
status_note: Effectively dormant: the CUDA code was last changed 2018-2021 and the January 2026 commits only zip MATLAB files; MIT-licensed and small (one ~1000-line .cu file), so it is easy to vendor or study but expect to port the build.
sources_read: WebSearch: 'Trajectory Optimized NUFFT' TRON Smith (summaries of onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/mrm.27497 and researchgate.net/publication/328349262)
